papers.title: The interventionist approach can address questions related to causes of effects if causes are considered as states instead of interventions.
papers.one_line: A conceptual argument that causes are states rather than interventions, concluding that a causes-of-outcomes question cannot be answered by any single target trial and instead requires effect decomposition synthesized across many trials that each emulate a different target trial.
papers.what_was_done: The sufficient causal set framework of Rothman is used to reframe what a target trial can and cannot deliver. The mathematics of the average causal effect is shown to compare outcome distributions under two physical states of the exposure variable, without reference to the mechanism that produced the state change, so a well-defined counterfactual requires a well-defined state and not a well-defined action. A worked example takes adiposity and mortality: diet, exercise and liposuction are three interventions that all lower adipose tissue, mediated through systemic inflammation and insulin sensitivity, and four distinct data-generating possibilities are enumerated that all reproduce the same total effect estimates from randomized trials of those three interventions. Distinguishing among the four requires additional trials that block the direct effect of each intervention, or observational data on the mediators with no unmeasured mediator-outcome confounding, or interaction terms; with the available data the estimate cannot be pinned down and only a range from sensitivity analysis is available. Body mass index is rejected as a component cause and therefore as a well-defined state. No data are analyzed and no effect estimate is reported.

future_research.gap: Answering what causes an outcome requires a synthesis architecture across trials of different interventions on the same intermediate construct, which does not exist as a method.
future_research.quote: Practically, this requires a synthesis of evidence across many different randomized trials investigating different interventions targeting the same intermediate construct

problems.evidence: The scientific target, whether adipose tissue causes mortality, is separated from what any single emulated protocol can deliver: three interventions that all reduce adiposity are compatible with four distinct causal structures, and identical trial estimates do not discriminate among them. The gap between the question asked and the protocol run is named as requiring decomposition across trials, which is exactly the accounting no single emulation reports.
problems.quote: Estimating the causes of outcomes (i.e. the common effect across multiple interventions) requires that the interventionist approach be expanded to include effect decomposition across many trials.

problems.evidence: Formulations of the same drug from different manufacturers differ in inactive ingredients and produce different adherence, yet are pooled into one treatment arm because the research question is said to tolerate that heterogeneity. Whether the tolerance is defensible is settled by declaring the level of detail the question requires; no procedure decides which formulations belong in the same class.
problems.quote: We understand that different companies have different “inactive” ingredients in their version of medication A, and these different formulations may lead to some participants adhering to the protocol more than others.
problems.locator: Sufficient Causal Framework and Well-Defined States

problems.evidence: The adiposity example lists exactly the questions a non-pharmaceutical protocol has to answer and cannot: which diet regimens, which exercise program, general or regional anesthesia for the liposuction, which depot the tissue comes from, brown or white. Each unresolved choice is a different treatment version, and the same worked example concludes that body mass index does not even name a well-defined state.
problems.quote: Is the liposuction under general or regional anesthesia, where is the adipose tissue being removed from?
problems.locator: Sufficient Causal Framework and Well-Defined States

problems.evidence: A single emulated trial is treated as informative only about the specific intervention it encodes; anything broader requires synthesis across emulations of different target trials. That is the missing extrapolation theory stated from the other direction: nothing licenses carrying a result from one successfully specified target trial to a different question.
problems.quote: evaluating the causes of effects/outcomes requires evidence synthesis across multiple studies that each emulate a different target randomized trial

problems.evidence: Four candidate mechanisms are simultaneously compatible with the data, and the response when the data cannot separate them is a sensitivity range rather than a point estimate. The mechanisms are not independent violations that can be varied one at a time: interaction between adiposity, diet, exercise and liposuction is the fourth possibility, and it changes the estimate only when the others are also entertained.
problems.quote: If we cannot distinguish between these mechanisms with the data available, we cannot obtain a precise estimate.
problems.locator: Sufficient Causal Framework and Well-Defined States

problems.evidence: The proposed resolution requires a target trial whose arms combine an intervention to reduce adipose tissue with a second intervention that eliminates the direct effect of diet, or of exercise, or of liposuction on mortality. These are joint strategies constructed for identification; the argument states they are theoretically possible while conceding that they demand substantive knowledge nobody currently has.
problems.quote: Every intervention is a complex intervention with many components and, to some extent, is ill-defined
problems.locator: Sufficient Causal Framework and Well-Defined States

papers.title: Strengthening inferential studies in the FDA Sentinel initiative: results from a methodological demonstration project.
papers.one_line: An FDA Sentinel demonstration emulating a target trial of SGLT-2 inhibitors versus DPP-4 inhibitors in 97,119 patients with type 2 diabetes, where replacing claims-code pancreatitis (positive predictive value 0.55 to 0.65) with an EHR phenotype (positive predictive value 0.90) moved the intention-to-treat hazard ratio from 0.99 (0.84 to 1.16) to 0.85 (0.67 to 1.07).
papers.what_was_done: A new-user active-comparator target trial was specified under the PRINCIPLED framework and posted publicly before analysis, then emulated in the Sentinel Real-World Evidence Data Enterprise using two partners: HealthVerity ambulatory records linked to closed claims for 2018 to 2020, and TriNetX records from 20 health care organizations linked to claims for 2013 to 2024. Cohort entry was first dispensing; 97,119 patients contributed. Acute pancreatitis was ascertained by a validated computable phenotype using diagnosis codes plus amylase, lipase and triglycerides, with natural language processing features added in TriNetX; at a fixed positive predictive value of 0.90 the phenotype reached sensitivity 0.88 without and 0.92 with text features. More than 135 variables entered propensity score fine stratification weights. Laboratory covariates were heavily incomplete: HbA1c was present for 29.4 percent of SGLT-2i and 27.3 percent of DPP-4i initiators in HealthVerity and about 50 percent in TriNetX, with serum creatinine and triglycerides present for 20 to 25 percent in HealthVerity. Missingness diagnostics via the smdi package supported missing at random, and 20 random-forest imputations were pooled by Rubin's rule. Pooled hazard ratios were 0.85 (0.67 to 1.07) for intention-to-treat and 0.84 (0.58 to 1.22) for per protocol in the claims plus EHR analysis, against 0.99 (0.84 to 1.16) and 0.94 (0.73 to 1.20) in the claims-only analysis. Ischemic stroke as a negative control outcome gave a pooled hazard ratio of 0.97 (0.82 to 1.14). The linked network covers roughly 25 million lives against 128.7 million in the claims-only Sentinel Distributed Database.

future_research.gap: The linked network is too small to give usable precision for rare outcomes; the conclusion of no difference may reflect power rather than equivalence.
future_research.quote: Future work integrating more data sources may be helpful in increasing the population size for the RWE-DE.

future_research.gap: Computable phenotypes deployed at new sites are not revalidated there, and no procedure exists for doing so in near real time.
future_research.quote: When resources permit, a smaller scale validation study using manual review of data from newer sites where the algorithm was applied may be considered.

problems.evidence: Two outcome definitions applied to the same cohort of 97,119 patients gave hazard ratios of 0.99 and 0.85, so the measurement instrument is shown to be a determinant of the answer rather than a background detail. What is not closed is any propagation of the phenotype's residual error into the interval: both estimates are reported as if the binary outcome were exact, and the 0.90 positive predictive value never enters the variance.
problems.quote: the estimates were closer to the null versus when using Sentinel’s phenotyping algorithm for pancreatitis with a PPV of 0.90

problems.evidence: The positivity check consists of distributional overlap, the weight distribution and post-weighting standardized differences across more than 135 covariates. Every one of those is a summary of the weights themselves; none of them names a patient history, such as a covariate pattern with no DPP-4i initiators, for which the comparison is unsupported.
problems.quote: As diagnostics for PS models, we evaluated distributional overlap, weight distribution, and individual covariate balance using standardized differences post-weighting.

problems.evidence: Requiring lab values to define the outcome forced the study off a 128.7 million member claims network onto a 25 million life linked network, and the surviving cohort of 97,119 produced a per-protocol interval spanning 0.58 to 1.22. The precision loss is attributed to the design restrictions rather than to the underlying database size, and no accounting of that loss is required before the study is run.
problems.quote: richer data from the claims-EHR linkages are obtained at the expense of a substantially smaller total available population size than claims-only networks

problems.evidence: A real diagnostic sequence is supplied: monotone missingness patterns, standardized differences between observed and missing groups with medians around 0.02 to 0.05, area under the curve for missingness prediction, and a test of association between the missingness indicator and pancreatitis. That closes the question of whether missing at random is defensible for these covariates. It does not treat the encounter process as causal structure: whether an HbA1c is drawn is itself a clinical decision downstream of health state, and the response is imputation of 70 percent of HealthVerity HbA1c values rather than modeling of the visit process.
problems.quote: multiple imputations are likely to provide best bias-variance trade-off

problems.evidence: Ischemic stroke is run as a negative control outcome and returns 0.97 (0.82 to 1.14), which is a concrete integration of one uncontrolled-confounding probe into a routine regulatory workflow. It stops there: no negative control exposure, no proxy variable and no validation subsample enters the analysis, and the null control result carries no calibration onto the pancreatitis interval.
problems.quote: The analysis of the stroke endpoint as a negative control outcome confirmed no difference in risk between SGLT-2i and DPP-4i

problems.evidence: The per-protocol estimand is defined by censoring at discontinuation or switching, and is then reported as a single Cox hazard ratio of 0.84 (0.58 to 1.22) alongside the intention-to-treat hazard ratio. The reported quantity is a hazard ratio under a proportional hazards model fitted in a weighted population; the estimand named in the protocol is the effect of adhering to the assigned strategy, and no reconciliation of the two is given.
problems.quote: In the weighted population, we estimated the hazard ratio for acute pancreatitis among initiators of SGLT-2i versus DPP-4i using Cox proportional hazards model.

problems.evidence: Estimates from HealthVerity and TriNetX are pooled, although the two partners cover different calendar windows (2018 to 2020 against 2013 to 2024), different care settings, and different laboratory capture, with HbA1c present for about 29 percent of HealthVerity patients against about 50 percent in TriNetX. The phenotype defining the outcome is itself acknowledged to behave differently across sites, so a pooled hazard ratio can average across emulations whose outcome variable does not mean the same thing.
problems.quote: validated computable phenotyping algorithms may show performance degradation at different sites

papers.title: Transparent reporting of observational studies emulating a target trial: the TARGET Statement.
papers.one_line: A 21-item consensus reporting checklist for target trial emulations, built from a 44-item candidate list through an 18-participant two-round survey, an 18-panelist consensus meeting and piloting with 108 users, scoped to parallel group emulations adjusted for baseline confounders.
papers.what_was_done: The guideline was developed under the EQUATOR framework in four stages: a systematic review of reporting in published emulations that identified 44 candidate items; a two-round online survey from August 2023 to March 2024 with 18 expert participants from six countries; a three-day consensus meeting in June 2024 with 18 panelists drawn from methodology, statistics, trials, epidemiology, clinical practice, evidence synthesis, industry and journal editing; and internal piloting with 13 and external piloting with 95 potential users from September 2024 to February 2025. The result is 21 items across abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion and other information. Items 6 and 7 are paired: 6a through 6h specify the target trial protocol component by component, and 7a through 7h describe how each was operationalized in the data, including 7g on identifying assumptions and 7h on the analysis plan and sensitivity analyses. Results items cover participant selection with a flow diagram, baseline characteristics by strategy, follow-up, missing data frequency, outcome frequency, effect estimates in both absolute and relative terms, and additional analyses. Other information covers ethics, registration, sharing of data and analytic code, funding and conflicts. Cloning and sequential trials are addressed only through counting conventions such as person-trials and clones in the flow diagram. Instrumental variable estimation and other non-confounder-control approaches are explicitly outside the scope.

future_research.gap: The checklist covers only the most common configuration and states that other settings, methods and assumptions in the field are not described by it.
future_research.quote: The guideline attempts to support comprehensive and clear reporting of analyses of observational data that explicitly emulate a target trial but does not describe all settings, methods, and assumptions that may be required in this evolving field.

problems.evidence: Item 18 is the only registration requirement in a 21-item checklist and asks for three facts: whether, when and where. Nothing asks which protocol versions were considered and dropped, so a registration that names one final target trial satisfies the item in full, and the alternatives that were rejected remain unrecorded even in an emulation that reports every other item.
problems.quote: State whether, when, and where the study protocol was registered.

problems.evidence: Item 7g requires each identifying assumption to be named for each estimand together with the variables that operationalize it, which forces assumptions onto the page instead of leaving them implicit. It stops short of a dashboard: no item asks which of those assumptions can be checked in the data and which cannot, so conditional exchangeability, positivity and sufficient definition of the strategies are all reported alike, and item 16 asks only for a narrative discussion of plausibility.
problems.quote: For each causal estimand, describe assumptions made to identify it, including assumptions regarding baseline confounding due to lack of randomization.

problems.evidence: Item 19 asks whether data, analytic code and other materials are accessible and how to reach them, which is the first checklist requirement of its kind for emulations. It is satisfied by a statement that materials are unavailable, and it names no specific artifact: phenotype logic, weight diagnostics and the rejected protocol versions are not enumerated anywhere in the 21 items.
problems.quote: Provide information on whether data, analytic code and/or other materials are accessible, and where and how they can be accessed.

problems.evidence: Positivity appears in the glossary as an identifying assumption, but the only results item that touches on it is item 9, which asks for baseline characteristics before and after weighting or matching. Covariate balance is a property of the weighted sample and says nothing about which covariate patterns had no one on one strategy; no item asks an emulation to name an unsupported patient history.
problems.quote: reporting baseline characteristics before and after adjustment for confounding

problems.evidence: Cloning and sequential trials enter the checklist only as a counting convention: report unique individuals alongside the total analyzed and label the latter person-trials or clones. Nothing asks how the variance was computed once a person appears in many trials or in both arms, so a checklist-complete report can leave the inference procedure for repeated contributions entirely undescribed.
problems.quote: Terms such as “person-trials” or “clones” can be helpful to differentiate numbers analyzed from unique individuals.

problems.evidence: Item 7b requires the grace period to be described as part of the treatment strategy, alongside decision rules for initiation and discontinuation. Description is all that is required: no item asks how the length of the grace period or the time grid was chosen, or whether that choice was made before outcomes were examined.
problems.quote: including any grace period after baseline within which interventions must be started and allowable reasons for discontinuation

problems.evidence: The document is a reporting instrument and says so: it describes what must appear, not what would be adequate. Item 14 asks that all sensitivity analyses be reported and item 16 that limitations be discussed, but neither sets a level of residual confounding, a degree of protocol mismatch, or a quantity of sensitivity analysis at which a study fails.
problems.quote: The guideline attempts to support comprehensive and clear reporting of analyses of observational data that explicitly emulate a target trial but does not describe all settings, methods, and assumptions that may be required in this evolving field.

problems.evidence: The scope is a parallel group emulation with confounder adjustment; instrumental variable estimation and other approaches to confounder control are declared out of scope and are said to require additional information that the checklist does not specify. Reporting requirements therefore attach to one estimation family by default, and no item asks whether a different estimator would have moved the answer.
problems.quote: The TARGET guideline does not, for example, specifically intend to guide the reporting of target trial emulations that use instrumental variable estimation

problems.evidence: Item 5 asks for original purpose, type, geography, setting and time period of each data source, plus linkage description. That is a provenance narrative. Nothing converts it into a fitness judgment, and no item defines a data property whose absence would stop the emulation rather than being written up under item 16.
problems.quote: Cite the data sources contributing to the analyses and for each one describe the following: original purpose, type, the geographical locations, setting, and time period.

papers.title: On the current and future potential of simulations based on directed acyclic graphs.
papers.one_line: Simulations from directed acyclic graphs at n = 1,000,000 show that minimal sufficient adjustment sets that graph theory declares equivalent are not equivalent in estimation: only the set made of direct ancestors of the outcome removes confounding bias from a logistic regression.
papers.what_was_done: Two demonstrations built on directed acyclic graphs are presented, with no empirical data and no treatment effect estimated. The first simulates three causal structures carrying four confounders each at n = 1,000,000, all nodes binary, an odds ratio of exp(1) on every arc and prevalence 0.5 in each node's reference category. For two of the three structures the graph identifies four distinct minimal sufficient adjustment sets of equal size, yet the logistic regression estimate is unbiased only for the set consisting of direct ancestors of the outcome; the residual bias from the more distant sets shrinks as the odds ratio moves toward 1.2, 1.5 and 2.0 but does not vanish. The second simulates selection at n = 10,000,000 where both exposure and outcome affect study participation, and reports the spurious risk difference across values of those two effects and across baseline participation probabilities, showing that even the sign of the bias is not predictable without external evidence on the parameters. The framing is that missingness of eligibility data compromises emulated target trial analysis through conditioning on the eligibility indicator and its missingness process. Available DAG simulation software is limited to binary data generated from logistic models; the R package dagR has been extended to risk-difference simulation, while time-to-event and repeated-measures generation remain unimplemented.

future_research.gap: DAG-based simulation software cannot generate longitudinal data with repeated measurements, so marginal structural model performance cannot be studied this way.
future_research.quote: future simulation algorithms should accomodate longitudinal data with repeated measurements

future_research.gap: No time-to-event data-generating algorithm exists in DAG-based simulation software.
future_research.quote: it would be especially useful to also implement time-to-event algorithms for DAG-based software

problems.evidence: A single graph yields four minimal sufficient adjustment sets of equal size, all of which close every backdoor path, yet at n = 1,000,000 with an arc odds ratio of exp(1) the logistic regression estimate is unbiased for only one of them. The analyst's choice among formally interchangeable options changes the answer, and nothing in the reported workflow requires an emulation to show which choice it made or what the alternatives would have produced.
problems.quote: The estimate obtained by logistic regression nonetheless will only be unbiased if one choses the MSAS consisting of the nodes being direct ancestors of the outcome, whereas adjusting for the more distant nodes is less effective in removing confounding bias.
problems.locator: Instructive use cases of DAG-based data simulations

problems.evidence: The stated motivation for building simulation infrastructure is that the conditions under which emulation reproduces a randomized estimate are unknown, so a set of successful reproductions carries no rule for the next question. The proposed remedy is simulation from a known causal truth, not extrapolation from past agreement.
problems.quote: it is not fully understood why the emulated target trial approach is better in some situations than in others, when it comes to reproducing the causal effect estimates from corresponding randomized controlled trials

problems.evidence: Proximity of an estimate to a gold-standard comparator is explicitly rejected as sufficient evidence about a procedure; the demand is for the conditions under which proximity holds, which requires the causal truth to be known. A binary agreed or disagreed label carries none of that information.
problems.quote: it is not sufficient to demonstrate that some algorithmic “blackbox” procedure yields an association estimate close to the effect estimate obtained by some gold standard comparison approach

problems.evidence: Missing eligibility information is treated as a structural problem, not a data gap: conditioning on the eligibility indicator and on its own missingness process opens biasing paths in the graph. That is a different object from a criterion that was recorded and met, and the graph makes the two distinguishable only if the missingness process is modeled explicitly.
problems.quote: including biasing paths induced by conditioning on the eligibility indicator and its missingness process

problems.evidence: At n = 10,000,000 with exposure and outcome both acting on participation and no direct exposure effect on outcome, the induced spurious risk difference changes sign and magnitude across the parameter grid. A cohort assembled through a healthcare-use or participation filter therefore cannot be assigned even a direction of bias without external knowledge of those two effects.
problems.quote: the magnitude and direction of the spurious risk difference introduced through selection bias vary widely depending on the effects of exposure and outcome on study participation
problems.locator: Instructive use cases of DAG-based data simulations

problems.evidence: Increasing model complexity is set against, not substituted for, causal knowledge: performance of a complex estimator can be evaluated only against a data-generating mechanism that is known, which is why the simulated truth is required. Flexibility in the estimator does not supply the structural knowledge that identification needs.
problems.quote: causal knowledge remains as fundamental for evaluating the performance of complex methods as it is for even the basic understanding of causal effects and different types of bias

papers.title: On the use of natural language processing to implement the target trial framework using unstructured data from the electronic health record.
papers.one_line: A review of natural language processing applied to each component of a target trial emulation in electronic health records, concluding that when adherence exists only as free-text self-report the practical response is to change the estimand to match the data.
papers.what_was_done: Each component of the target trial protocol is walked through against the electronic health record, with published applications supplying the numbers. Rule-based extraction of arthralgia reached a positive predictive value of 90 percent and sensitivity of 83 percent against manual chart review, while ICD-9 coding reached 79 percent and 52 percent for the same condition. A large language model applied to free-text notes recovered health-related social needs at recall between 62.93 for barriers to care and 91.92 for transition of care, none of which appear in structured fields. Extraction of cancer stage from oncology notes attenuated a previously reported association between COVID-19 infection and mortality once stage was adjusted for. The running use case is long-acting versus daily oral antiretroviral therapy among adults with housing insecurity, where eligibility, exposure, adherence and confounders each sit partly in narrative text. Up to 80 percent of electronic health record content is estimated to be unstructured, and a systematic review of 519 natural language processing studies published between January 2022 and February 2024 found only 5 percent used real patient care data. Extracted text is also unequal: negative patient descriptors occur 2.54 times more often in the notes of patients identified as Black than of patients identified as White.

future_research.gap: External validation of a text-extraction algorithm does not transfer across sites, because record structure and documentation habits differ.
future_research.quote: even if an algorithm has been validated in previous studies, we advise researchers to test it on their own data

future_research.gap: The extraction literature is almost entirely methodological; real patient-care data are scarce as training and evaluation material.
future_research.quote: yet more applied examples are needed as are real patient data that can be used to train these models

problems.evidence: When adherence in the antiretroviral use case exists only as periodic free-text self-report, the recommended responses are to switch estimand, drop the protocol component, or run a bias analysis. Switching estimand silently replaces the intended per-protocol effect with a different, data-defined quantity, and nothing in the workflow records that the substitution happened or what it cost.
problems.quote: The investigators may have to choose a different estimand that aligns with the data available, forgo that TTF criterion, or perform a quantitative bias analysis to estimate the impact of the systematic error
problems.locator: Causal contrasts of interest and analytic effect

problems.evidence: Every extraction figure reported here, from 90 percent positive predictive value for arthralgia down to 62.93 recall for barriers to care, is a measurement with error, yet the extracted variable enters the emulation as a binary indicator. The error in the text itself compounds the extraction error and is not quantified by any of the validation studies cited.
problems.quote: The validity of NLP output assumes that the underlying free text data were captured without error, and we know this to not be the case with EHR data

problems.evidence: Cancer stage extracted from oncology notes is used as a confounder, and stage is described as changing during treatment and as influencing subsequent prescribing. A note-derived variable therefore carries information written after treatment started, so the boundary between a baseline adjustment variable and a post-treatment variable is set by the date of the note rather than by the structure of the extraction.
problems.quote: Cancer staging, an important prognostic factor, changes throughout the course of treatment, which can impact a provider's treatment decision and the patient's outcome.
problems.locator: Causal contrasts of interest and analytic effect

problems.evidence: The narrative substrate from which covariates and outcomes are extracted differs by patient race, with negative descriptors 2.54 times more frequent in the notes of Black patients. Any subgroup estimate built on note-derived variables therefore rests on a measurement process whose error rate varies with the grouping variable, and no reported diagnostic separates that from a real subgroup effect.
problems.quote: negative patient descriptors were 2.54 times more likely to occur in history and physical notes of patients who identified as Black compared to patients who identified as White

problems.evidence: Release of extraction source code and its documentation is asked for explicitly, which names one of the missing artifacts. It remains an exhortation with no reporting requirement and no mechanism, and it covers only the extraction code; weight diagnostics and rejected protocol versions are not mentioned.
problems.quote: releasing their source codes and accompanying documentation for their NLP solutions so that others may learn from these examples

problems.evidence: Fitness of the record for the question is stated as the governing constraint on emulation quality, yet the conclusion supplies no measurement of closeness and no threshold below which the emulation should not proceed. The 519-study review finding that only 5 percent used real patient care data shows the same gap upstream in the extraction literature.
problems.quote: The quality of the emulation will ultimately be governed by how close the EHR data, whether structured or unstructured, allow for approximation of the target trial.

papers.title: The target trial framework in global health research: barriers and opportunities.
papers.one_line: A scoping review of 391 target trial emulations finding that four high-income countries supply 60 percent of the data and low- and middle-income countries only 6 percent, with 6 percent of first authors and 4 percent of senior authors based in a low- or middle-income country.
papers.what_was_done: A search returned 1432 non-duplicate records, 480 went to full text and 391 met the selection criteria. Annual output rose from 14 studies in 2020 to 126 in 2023, with the growth almost entirely from high-income data sources. Data provenance was counted by country: 147 studies used data from the USA, 42 from the UK, 24 from Sweden, 23 from Denmark, and 34 were multi-country; those four countries alone account for 60 percent of the total. Botswana, Brazil, China, Iran and Thailand are the only low- and middle-income countries contributing data, 6 percent of studies, with 12 further multi-country studies including some such data. Twenty-five studies had a first author and 16 a senior author based in a low- or middle-income country, and in every multi-country study both first and last authors were affiliated with high-income institutions. Two barriers are named: routinely collected data that are absent or of poor quality, and few trained researchers. The proposed remedy is to attach observational data collection to the infrastructure of large randomized trials already running in these settings, using the E-MOTIVE trial across 78 hospitals in Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa and Tanzania with 210,132 vaginal deliveries as the worked case, and a heat-exposure analysis nested in the 16-hospital ALERT trial as an existing example. Regional databases, preprints and conference abstracts were excluded, which the review states will have inflated the high-income share.

future_research.gap: Labeling a study a target trial emulation does not establish that the framework was applied correctly, and the review had no way to check.
future_research.quote: While several studies explicitly reported the utilisation of the target trial framework, this does not guarantee that the framework was correctly implemented.

problems.evidence: All 391 studies were classified by whether they said they used the framework, and the review states plainly that the label does not establish correct implementation. No verification was attempted across the whole set, which is precisely the substitution of a name for an assessment of the assumption burden.
problems.quote: While several studies explicitly reported the utilisation of the target trial framework, this does not guarantee that the framework was correctly implemented.

problems.evidence: Data fitness is treated as a binary practical obstacle described in narrative terms: sources are lacking or of poor quality, systems are fragmented, and patients see multiple providers at their discretion. The conclusion is that valid work is impossible without adequate data, but no measurable criterion is offered by which an investigator could decide a given source fails, so 391 studies proceeded without one.
problems.quote: Without easy and affordable access to high-quality data, it is impossible for researchers to carry out well-designed, bias-free observational studies.
problems.locator: WHY HAVE SO FEW APPLICATIONS OF THE TARGET TRIAL FRAMEWORK USED DATA FROM LOW- AND MIDDLE-INCOME COUNTRIES?

problems.evidence: The corpus that supports claims about how well emulation works is drawn from four countries for 60 percent of its volume, with 6 percent from low- and middle-income settings. Any confidence that emulation transfers to a new setting rests on a body of evidence whose data provenance is that narrow, and the review supplies no argument for the transfer.
problems.quote: Studies using data from the USA, the UK, Denmark, and Sweden (all high-income countries) accounted for over half (60%) of all studies that utilized the target trial framework worldwide.

problems.evidence: The argument for observational work in these settings is that trial populations are restricted by consent barriers such as illiteracy and language, so the trial estimate is not the effect in everyone eligible. The observational alternative is asserted to be more representative because consent is handled at data collection, and no sampling model or accounting is offered for the step from the analyzed sample to the target population.
problems.quote: the treatment effect estimated within those that were eligible and gave informed consent may not reflect the true treatment effect in the ‘target population’ of everyone eligible to participate
problems.locator: WHAT BENEFITS CAN INCREASED USE OF THE TARGET TRIAL FRAMEWORK BRING TO GLOBAL HEALTH RESEARCH?

problems.evidence: The proposed pooling routes, collaborative initiatives that combine individual data from many countries, are described as needing integration across local, national and international data managers. Quality of the underlying records is stated to vary between settings, so a merged dataset can carry the same field name with different meaning across contributors, and no harmonization check is specified.
problems.quote: Disparities in quality of data across LMICs can affect the ability to address locally relevant problems and reduce the generalisability of findings.
problems.locator: WHY HAVE SO FEW APPLICATIONS OF THE TARGET TRIAL FRAMEWORK USED DATA FROM LOW- AND MIDDLE-INCOME COUNTRIES?

papers.title: Assessing Wolbachia-mediated sterility for dengue control: emulation of a cluster-randomized target trial in Singapore.
papers.one_line: A cluster-randomized test-negative target trial emulated across 16 Singapore townships and 133,821 dengue-tested individuals, reporting protective efficacy of 47 percent, 44 percent and 61 percent after 3, 6 and at least 12 months of Wolbachia male mosquito releases.
papers.what_was_done: A two-arm cluster-randomized test-negative controlled trial was specified for epidemiological week 1 of 2019 through week 26 of 2022 and emulated in the national dengue testing database. Four townships already receiving long-term wAlbB male releases formed the intervention arm; 12 control townships were drawn from 26 candidates by constrained randomization so that historical dengue incidence for 2010 to 2016 matched between arms at a 1 to 3 ratio. Of 133,821 individuals tested for febrile illness by RT-qPCR, NS1 or IgM through general practitioners, polyclinics and hospitals, those with addresses in more than one township, conflicting laboratory results, or fewer than three months of exposure were excluded. Environmental, anthropogenic and socioeconomic covariates including house prices and building age entered propensity weights, followed by weighted logistic regression with cluster bootstrap at township level. Intention-to-treat protective efficacies were 47 percent (25 to 69), 44 percent (33 to 77) and 61 percent (38 to 78) for 3, 6 and at least 12 months of exposure, and ranged from 49 percent (13 to 72) to 77 percent (60 to 94) across years at the longest exposure. Nine sensitivity analyses were run, including 1000 re-randomizations of the control allocation, in-space placebo assignment of each control town, in-time placebo periods 52 and 104 weeks before intervention, sector-level bootstrap, and an alternative propensity score matching procedure with exact matching on calendar time. Movement of mosquitoes or people between adjacent townships is not analyzed.

future_research.gap: Entomological exposure could not be linked to protective efficacy because vector surveillance coverage was incomplete for most of the study window.
future_research.quote: it was difficult to directly examine the relationship between protective efficacies and Aedes abundance as proxied by the Gravitrap index in our study

problems.evidence: The four intervention townships were fixed by an existing program, so the emulated randomization was constructed afterward by selecting 12 controls out of 26 candidates conditional on matching 2010 to 2016 dengue incidence. The target trial being emulated is therefore defined by a balancing criterion computed from the same historical series that determines the arms, and inference proceeds as though that trial had been fixed in advance.
problems.quote: While four long-term Wolbachia field trial townships were not randomly pre-selected, we emulated constrained randomization protocols for cluster-randomized trials by randomly selecting a set of 12 control townships
problems.locator: Emulating randomization protocols from cluster-randomized trials for Wolbachia interventions

problems.evidence: Exposure is assigned by residential township for an intervention that works by suppressing a flying vector population. Individuals with addresses in two townships are dropped rather than modeled, which removes the clearest cases of ambiguous exposure without addressing the underlying issue: a resident of a control town adjacent to an intervention town is treated as unexposed, and no analysis bounds the resulting spillover.
problems.quote: We excluded individuals who had more than one residential address in different control or intervention townships and individuals who had been tested at different laboratories with conflicting dengue results.

problems.evidence: The assignment unit is an administrative planning area used by government ministries, chosen because it is the boundary on which the program operates rather than because it delimits transmission. Treatment version varies with release volume, duration and the timing of expansion to new towns; the reduced efficacy in later years is attributed to expansion into Choa Chu Kang, which shows the version changed during the study.
problems.quote: Twenty-six townships in Singapore that were not subject to Wolbachia interventions were considered potential locations as control sites.
problems.locator: Emulating randomization protocols from cluster-randomized trials for Wolbachia interventions

problems.evidence: Three exposure durations are reported as three efficacies: 47 percent at 3 months, 44 percent at 6 months and 61 percent at 12 months or more. Duration is treated as an exposure gradient, but no rule places releases of different intensity, coverage or start date within a single treatment version, and the non-monotone drop from 47 to 44 percent is not attributable to any stated version difference.
problems.quote: Intention-to-treat analyses revealed that, compared with controls, Wolbachia releases for 3, 6 and ≥12 months was associated to 47% (95% confidence interval: 25–69%), 44% (33–77%) and 61% (38–78%) protective efficacy against dengue, respectively.

problems.evidence: The whole treated arm consists of four clusters, and the stated purpose of constrained randomization is to prevent chance imbalance arising from that number. Positivity at the level that matters here, the cluster, cannot be assessed by any weight summary; the reported diagnostics are covariate balance and re-randomization distributions, and no analysis names a township profile for which no counterfactual arm exists.
problems.quote: The constrained randomization procedure also helped to prevent chance imbalance in baseline dengue risk due to the small number of intervention
problems.locator: Emulating randomization protocols from cluster-randomized trials for Wolbachia interventions

problems.evidence: Two families of negative control are built into the workflow: in-space placebo assignment treating each control town as if intervened, whose odds ratios centered on 1, and in-time placebo intervention periods 52 and 104 weeks before releases began, which produced no protective effect. That is a concrete integration of falsification tests into an emulation. It does not extend to proxies or a validation subsample, and no calibration carries the null control results onto the 61 percent estimate.
problems.quote: we conducted in-time placebo checks on intervention sites, where we took placebo interventions in the actual intervention site before the intervention began

problems.evidence: Nine sensitivity analyses each perturb one element: covariate set, control allocation, weighting, bootstrap resolution, matching procedure, placebo site, placebo period. None combines a violation of the no-interference assumption with residual environmental confounding and the staggered adoption timing, which is the configuration the discussion concedes is plausible, so robustness is demonstrated one assumption at a time.
problems.quote: We conducted a battery of sensitivity analyses to ensure the robustness of our model estimates.

problems.evidence: Exposure is cut at 3, 6 and 12 months and a minimum of 3 months of exposure is imposed for eligibility, while releases began at different calendar dates across the four towns. The defense of these cuts is that a study window spanning 2019 to 2022 averages over epidemic and inter-epidemic seasons; no outcome-blind rule set the three thresholds or the three-month minimum.
problems.quote: the staggered adoption setting of the field trials mean that exposed and unexposed individuals are enrolled at varying time points, which may lead to biases if there were temporal variations in dengue incidence

papers.title: Core Concepts in Pharmacoepidemiology: New-User Designs.
papers.one_line: A tutorial mapping the new-user versus non-user, active comparator new-user and prevalent new-user designs onto three distinct target trials, stating that lag periods and the decisions made inside them change the causal question rather than merely the precision.
papers.what_was_done: Three pharmacoepidemiologic designs are recast as emulations of three different target trials, worked through a hormone replacement therapy example in which a hypothetical new agent, Newstogen, has shown cardiovascular benefit in a placebo-controlled phase III trial. The new-user versus non-user design emulates initiation versus no therapy, requires a washout period such as 12 months with no relevant prescriptions and a look-back window at least as long, and is credited with avoiding depletion of susceptibles, left truncation, adjustment for intermediates and immortal time. The active comparator new-user design emulates initiation of one agent versus a therapeutic alternative at clinical equipoise, requires naivety to both, and is noted to shrink the available sample because new use is needed in both arms. The prevalent new-user design admits switchers by constructing exposure sets that pair prevalent new users with continuers matched on exposure history, distinguishing direct, delayed and complex switchers, and re-applying eligibility at each refill. Failure modes are enumerated for each: an inappropriate comparator leaves confounding by indication, too short a washout leaves depletion of susceptibles, badly built exposure sets reintroduce left truncation, and differential surveillance separates switchers from continuers. Dynamic and time-varying strategies, and the estimation required for per-protocol effects, are explicitly outside scope. No data are analyzed.

future_research.gap: Only static interventions are covered; dynamic and time-varying treatment strategies are left to other work.
future_research.quote: we limited our discussion to questions pertaining to static interventions and did not consider dynamic or time‐varying treatment strategies

future_research.gap: Estimating the effect of following a strategy rather than starting it requires methods the tutorial does not supply.
future_research.quote: These questions necessitate approaches that require additional statistical considerations beyond the scope of this article

problems.evidence: A lag period is introduced to blunt detection bias, for instance starting person-time and event counting six months after initiation. The tutorial states directly that the lag and the choices made inside it change the causal question, not just the estimate, so a component chosen for measurement reasons silently redefines the estimand.
problems.quote: Furthermore, lag periods (and the decisions made during them) can modify the causal question under study.

problems.evidence: Prevalent new-user studies require decisions on matching or stratification windows, on which switcher class defines the study population, and on grace period lengths that separate direct from delayed switchers. All three are described as consequential and left to careful consideration; no procedure fixes them without reference to the outcome.
problems.quote: researchers need to carefully consider the appropriate time windows for matching or stratification, which types of switchers (direct vs. delayed vs. complex) represent the most appropriate study population, and what types of grace periods adequately capture the difference between these varying types

problems.evidence: Switchers are sorted into direct, delayed and complex classes, and the recommendation for the Newstogen example is to keep only direct switchers. The class boundaries are set by grace period length, and the tutorial concedes that each boundary encodes a different assumption about how exposure history relates to switching and to the outcome, with no rule for choosing among them.
problems.quote: Different decisions reflect different assumptions about the association between exposure history, switching, and the outcome.

problems.evidence: Differential surveillance between switchers and continuers is addressed by requiring the comparator to have had a general practice visit within three months of the switcher's prescription. A healthcare-contact requirement is itself an eligibility criterion built from a healthcare-use variable that is caused by health state, so the fix for one measurement problem installs a selection node in the design.
problems.quote: This concern can be mitigated by adding a healthcare‐contact component to the exposure set definition, for example, comparators are required to have a general practice visit within 3 months of the switcher prescription.

problems.evidence: Requiring new use in both arms compounds a restriction that already reduces the analyzable population, and the prevalent new-user design was introduced partly to recover sample size for recently marketed drugs. The tutorial identifies the loss but supplies no accounting of how many patients survive the washout, look-back and exposure set construction relative to the source database.
problems.quote: the sample size limitation encountered by new user studies is only exacerbated in the context of an active comparator new user study, where new use is required in both treatment and comparator

problems.evidence: Matching, weighting and outcome modeling are listed as alternatives whose selection becomes harder once exposure sets are involved, with no criterion given for the choice. The consequence is stated concretely: if exposure sets are not suitably implemented, left truncation and depletion of susceptibles return, so the estimator choice determines whether the design's central protection holds.
problems.quote: the selection of analytic methods (matching vs. weighting vs. outcome modeling) becomes more complex due to the need to incorporate the exposure sets

problems.evidence: Sequential trial and clone-censor-weight approaches are recommended as the general solution to defining follow-up start for non-users, precisely because they let the same patient enter more than once. The tutorial records the efficiency motive and none of the cost: repeated participation and calendar-time structure are not mentioned as things the resulting inference must handle.
problems.quote: more general solutions (that allow the same patient to be considered for inclusion multiple times) include using sequential trial designs or clone‐censor‐weighting approaches

problems.evidence: The hormone replacement therapy case is presented as the canonical discordance between observational studies and the Women's Health Initiative, resolved by a single narrative explanation about exposed versus unexposed person-time structure. It is a verdict on agreement, not a calibrated comparison: no quantitative decomposition attributes the gap between the observational and trial estimands to the design features named.
problems.quote: did not properly correspond to a hypothetical target trial and introduced a variety of potential biases

papers.title: Four targets: an enhanced framework for guiding causal inference from observational data.
papers.one_line: A framework adding target estimand, target population and target validity around target trial emulation, stating that the estimator chosen for confounding control changes the population the effect applies to and that a meticulous emulation may not recover the true effect even in its own study sample.
papers.what_was_done: Four concepts are linked into one workflow and illustrated with buprenorphine dosing for opioid use disorder in Veterans Affairs data. The target estimand is specified through the five ICH E9 (R1) elements, with intercurrent events handled by one of five strategies; here the estimand is the 2-year intention-to-treat and per-protocol risk differences and hazard ratios for higher-dose (24 to 32 mg per day) against standard-dose (16 to 24 mg per day) buprenorphine on retention, hospitalization and all-cause mortality. The target population is everyone in Veterans Affairs diagnosed with opioid use disorder, while the study sample is only those who received buprenorphine, under 20 percent of that population, and the two differ on patient preference, age, race and ethnicity, socioeconomic status, psychiatric comorbidity and pain. The target trial section covers sequential nested trials on an alternative time scale and clone-censor-weight for grace periods such as initiation within 28 days of supervised withdrawal. Target validity is defined as a joint measure over internal and external validity with respect to a named population and estimand, with target bias its complement. Different confounding-control methods are enumerated as targeting different populations: inverse probability weighting the whole study sample, matching the treated or untreated, overlap weights the equipoise population, instrumental variables the compliers. No data are analyzed and no estimate is produced.

future_research.gap: Which population a target trial emulation actually speaks to is unresolved and rarely raised in the literature.
future_research.quote: even when meticulously conducted, the effect estimate obtained from target trial emulation may not represent the true effect in the study sample, much less the true effect in the target population

future_research.gap: Emulation does not remove unmeasured confounding, and the residual burden is left to sensitivity analysis.
future_research.quote: target trial emulation, like any other observational analysis, can suffer from unmeasured (or uncontrolled) confounding

problems.evidence: Five estimation approaches are laid side by side and each is shown to answer a different question: inverse probability weighting the whole sample, matching the treated or the untreated, overlap weights the equipoise population, instrumental variables an unenumerable set of compliers. Nothing selects among them on principle, and no requirement exists that a study show whether its choice changed the population its estimate describes.
problems.quote: different statistical methods to control for confounding may correspond to different populations to which the treatment effect applies

problems.evidence: Clone-censor-weight and sequential nested trials are named as changing the analyzed sample itself, because a person appears many times and the resulting distribution of characteristics, some of them effect modifiers, differs from the source population. The efficiency of repeated participation is therefore bought at the cost of an altered estimand, and the framework flags this as underappreciated rather than solved.
problems.quote: both approaches allow study participants to be included in the analysis multiple times, which will change the sample being analysed and subsequently alter the distribution of participant characteristics

problems.evidence: Sampling weights, outcome regression and doubly robust estimators are proposed to carry the buprenorphine estimate from the treated sample to all veterans with opioid use disorder, and the framework insists on naming the target population before emulating. What it does not supply is any accounting: the transport assumptions are stacked on top of the confounding assumptions with no statement of the combined burden, and the resulting quantity has no reported sensitivity to either layer.
problems.quote: even when meticulously conducted, the effect estimate obtained from target trial emulation may not represent the true effect in the study sample, much less the true effect in the target population

problems.evidence: The framework asks explicitly that any difference between the estimand and population of the research question and the estimand and population imposed by design and analysis be noted and accounted for, which is the decomposition the registry entry describes. It stops at an instruction: no measure, no partition of the total gap into scientific-target mismatch, protocol compromise, mapping loss and estimation error, and no worked example showing the sizes.
problems.quote: Any additional differences between the target population and target estimand specified in the research question, and the population or estimand implied or imposed by the study design or data analysis, should be noted and accounted for.

problems.evidence: Intercurrent event strategies are said to carry different identification assumptions, with some resulting effects identifiable from the observational data and others not. That distinction is exactly what an assumption dashboard would surface, and the recommendation stops at including the strategy alongside the estimand; nothing marks which of the reported quantities rests on an assumption that cannot be checked.
problems.quote: Different strategies for handling intercurrent events may require different sets of identification assumptions and lead to different treatment effects, some of which are identifiable from the observational data and others are not.

problems.evidence: The analyzable sample is under 20 percent of the target population, because outcomes under either dosing strategy exist only for people who received buprenorphine at all. The restriction is imposed by the treatment comparison rather than by data volume, and the framework notes the two groups differ on multiple effect modifiers without quantifying what the restriction costs.
problems.quote: the study sample is only those in the VA who were diagnosed with OUD and also received buprenorphine

problems.evidence: Truncation by death is listed as an intercurrent event to be handled by an explicit estimand strategy, which places it among the identification decisions rather than among data preparation steps. The framework does not go further: it names five strategies without saying which is defensible when death is a competing event, and the buprenorphine estimand includes all-cause mortality as an outcome without addressing the other endpoints truncated by it.
problems.quote: including treatment discontinuation, protocol deviations, and truncation by death

papers.title: Enhancing inferences and conclusions in body image focused non-experimental research via a causal modelling approach: A tutorial.
papers.one_line: A tutorial applying the target trial framework to body image research, where an intervention defined as inducing appearance comparison to fitspiration content is emulated by a single self-report Likert item split at Sometimes versus Never.
papers.what_was_done: The counterfactual framework, identifiability assumptions and causal diagrams are introduced non-technically and applied to one worked question: whether appearance comparisons to fitspiration content on Instagram cause dietary restraint. The target trial specifies women aged 18 or older with eating disorder symptoms who view fitspiration content in 2021, randomized to an intervention that induces any appearance comparison versus no intervention, followed for 8 months to the dietary restraint subscale of the EDE-Q. Emulation replaces each component with what the survey contains: eating disorder symptoms become the presence of any of four behaviors (binge eating, excessive exercise, vomiting, laxative use); the treatment strategy becomes endorsement of Sometimes through Always on one item asking how often the respondent compares her appearance to same-sex fitspiration images, against Never; positivity is addressed by restricting to women who already view the content. The tutorial states that only one item measuring the exposure was available, that self-report will not capture all comparisons, and that a different cut point such as Always versus Never to Sometimes is possible but must stay conceptually aligned with the ideal intervention. The demonstration uses simulated data with no missing values and no loss to follow-up, and Stata and R code plus the simulated data are posted on the Open Science Framework.

future_research.gap: Full emulation of every protocol component is conceded to be routinely impossible, and what remains is articulation of the compromises rather than a measure of what they cost.
future_research.quote: it is not always possible to emulate every element of the idealised trial
future_research.locator: The target trial framework in causal identification

problems.evidence: The intervention is an unspecified action that induces appearance comparison, compared against no intervention. Neither the version of the intervention nor the mechanism by which comparison would be induced or removed is stated, and the unit of assignment is an individual whose exposure comes from her own social media use. This is exactly a behavioral target trial whose treatment versions are undefined at specification time.
problems.quote: We define the target trial intervention as an intervention that induces ‘appearance comparison to fitspiration content on Instagram’, with the comparator arm as no intervention.

problems.evidence: The specified strategy removes all appearance comparisons to fitspiration content; the emulated strategy is endorsement of Never on one survey item. Self-report is conceded not to capture all comparisons, so what is estimated is a contrast between response categories on an instrument, a different quantity from the specified intervention rather than a noisy measurement of it.
problems.quote: There is a possibility of measurement bias in this indicator, as selfreported comparisons may not encompass (whether intentionally or unintentionally) all cases of ‘appearance comparisons to fitspiration content’.

problems.evidence: Complete removal of appearance comparisons and partial reduction are offered as alternative strategies, and the cut point that separates the arms could be placed at Sometimes or at Always. The stated criterion for choosing is conceptual alignment with the ideal intervention, which is a judgment rather than a procedure, so the equivalence class of behaviors counted as treated is set by the analyst.
problems.quote: Importantly, this treatment strategy represents an ideal scenario in which all ‘appearance comparisons to fitspiration content on Instagram’ are removed.

problems.evidence: The exposure rests on one questionnaire item and no second measure exists in the data against which to run the sensitivity analysis the tutorial itself recommends. The dichotomized response then enters the analysis as a binary treatment indicator with no error model, and validation would require an instrument the study does not have.
problems.quote: In our case, we only had a single item available that measured ‘appearance comparisons to fitspiration content’.

problems.evidence: Positivity is handled by narrowing the eligible population to women who already view fitspiration content, described as increasing the chances of fulfilling the assumption. No diagnostic follows: nothing reports which covariate profiles among those women still have no one in one arm, and the phrase increase the chances is the whole of the evidence offered.
problems.quote: We have also limited the sample to women that view fitspiration content presented on Instagram, to increase the chances of fulfilling the positivity assumption.

problems.evidence: The eligibility criterion is eating disorder symptoms; the operationalization is the reported presence of four behaviors. A woman with restricting or purging behavior outside those four is recorded identically to a woman with no symptoms at all, so failing the criterion and having no record of it are the same event in the data.
problems.quote: the restriction to those with eating disorder symptoms is limited to reporting the presence of four specific behaviours (binge eating, excessive exercise, vomiting, and laxative use) and may therefore not capture people with other eating disorder

problems.evidence: The worked demonstration assumes no missing data and no loss to follow-up over 8 months, and the tutorial notes that dropout related to eating disorder severity would induce selection bias in a realistic dataset. The observation process is therefore acknowledged as causally relevant and then removed by assumption rather than modeled.
problems.quote: although our current example assumes no missing data or loss to followup, it is vital to acknowledge that in a more realistic dataset, such circumstance could induce selection bias

problems.evidence: Annotated Stata and R code and the simulated data are deposited publicly, which is more than most emulations release and makes the operationalization of each protocol component inspectable. What is deposited is a teaching demonstration on simulated data: no phenotype logic, no weight diagnostics and no record of the protocol variants that were considered and dropped.
problems.quote: The simulated data and Stata and R code for a step-by-step demonstration on how to estimate the ACE can be found on the Open Science Framework

papers.title: Estimating the Effect of Bariatric Surgery on Cardiovascular Events Using Observational Data?
papers.one_line: Two target trials of bariatric surgery emulated in US veterans data, where the 7-year cardiovascular risk difference was −0.9 percentage points (95 percent CI −12.0 to 14.0) and −1.4 (−5.1 to 3.2), against −5.1 (0.4 to 10.7) from the conventional analysis of the same data.
papers.what_was_done: Two target trials among veterans with diabetes were specified: trial 1 randomizes bariatric operation versus no operation among people who have already completed preoperative preparation, trial 2 randomizes preoperative preparation plus operation versus neither. Trial 1 pooled 8087 eligible individuals across sequential trials, contributing 198,832 person-trials, of whom 435 underwent surgery (63 percent sleeve gastrectomy, 28 percent gastric bypass). The 7-year cardiovascular risk was 18.0 percent (6.9 to 32.7) with surgery and 18.9 percent (17.7 to 20.1) without, a difference of −0.9 percentage points (−12.0 to 14.0). Trial 2 covered 10,065 individuals and gave 17.4 percent (13.6 to 22.0) against 18.8 percent (17.8 to 19.9), a difference of −1.4 (−5.1 to 3.2). Benchmarking against randomized trials on positive control outcomes gave 5-year BMI differences of −3.4 and −2.0 kg per square meter against trial values of −5.7 and −4.3, and HbA1c differences of −0.57 and −0.53 against −0.4 and −1.7. Neither trial could be emulated cleanly: essentially everyone completing preoperative preparation proceeds to surgery, and the start of the preoperative period is not recorded, so trial 2 required assuming a 6 to 12 month preoperative window with cloning and censoring. Preoperative evaluation also measured comorbidities differentially, with an additional 32 percent of the surgery group versus 6 percent of the no-surgery group diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea in the year before baseline. The conventional analysis of the same data reproduced the protective association reported by prior meta-analyses at relative risks near 0.5.

future_research.gap: No observational data source records the date at which bariatric surgery was first considered, and without it neither target trial can be emulated cleanly.
future_research.quote: A pure comparison of individuals who do and do not experience a preoperative period is not possible using these electronic health records, which is a major barrier to target trial emulation.
future_research.locator: CHALLENGES TO THE EMULATION OF TARGET TRIAL #2

problems.evidence: The positivity failure here is structural and is named in words rather than found by a diagnostic: the arm consisting of people who complete preoperative preparation and then do not have surgery is essentially empty. No weight distribution or standardized difference would have surfaced this, and the response was to redefine the trial, not to report a statistic.
problems.quote: Target trial #1 cannot be directly emulated using available observational data because essentially everybody who successfully completes the preoperative component receives surgery.
problems.locator: CHALLENGES TO THE EMULATION OF TARGET TRIAL #1

problems.evidence: Time of assignment is the protocol component that the record does not contain, so it is replaced by an assumed preoperative duration of more than 6 and less than 12 months, enforced by censoring clones who operate outside that window. Most clones assigned to surgery remain uncensored through a period that is not a real preoperative period, so the emulated contrast is defined by the assumed window rather than by the intended one.
problems.quote: we could assume a certain expected duration of the preoperative components, such as more than 6 months but less than 12 months
problems.locator: CHALLENGES TO THE EMULATION OF TARGET TRIAL #2

problems.evidence: To restore overlap, eligibility was narrowed on covariate trajectory: former or never smokers, no BMI increase above 2 units in the prior year, HbA1c change between −2 and 2. These criteria are computed from repeated clinical measurements, so they select on healthcare contact, and the paper states that weight loss in the untreated arm may itself signal undiagnosed chronic disease. Selecting on such a variable conditions on a descendant of the outcome's causes.
problems.quote: weight loss in the no-surgery group may be the unintentional consequence of undiagnosed chronic disease
problems.locator: CHALLENGES TO THE EMULATION OF TARGET TRIAL #1

problems.evidence: The preoperative workup is itself an encounter-generating process tied to one arm: in the year before baseline an additional 32 percent of the surgery group versus 6 percent of the no-surgery group received a sleep apnea diagnosis, with parallel gaps for osteoarthritis, hypertension and dyslipidemia. Confounders and exclusion criteria are therefore ascertained by different processes in the two arms, and imputing the values would not repair a difference that lies in who was looked at.
problems.quote: As a result of the preoperative evaluation, individuals in the surgery group may have comorbidities measured more frequently than individuals in the no-surgery group.

problems.evidence: A national veterans database yields 8087 eligible individuals and 198,832 person-trials, but only 435 surgeries, and the resulting 7-year risk difference spans −12.0 to 14.0 percentage points. The eligibility restrictions imposed to secure overlap are what produce that effective sample, and the interval is compatible with both a large benefit and a large harm.
problems.quote: Of 8087 eligible individuals pooled across sequential trials (198,832 person-trials), 435 underwent surgery
problems.locator: AN APPLICATION TO US VETERANS DATA

problems.evidence: The 8087 individuals contribute 198,832 person-trials, so each person enters roughly 25 sequential trials, and trial 2 additionally clones every eligible person into both strategies. The efficiency of that expansion is what makes 435 surgeries analyzable at all; the repeated contribution of the same person across calendar time is not accompanied by any reported treatment of the induced dependence.
problems.quote: Of 8087 eligible individuals pooled across sequential trials (198,832 person-trials), 435 underwent surgery
problems.locator: AN APPLICATION TO US VETERANS DATA

problems.evidence: Benchmarking against randomized trials is reported as approximately successful for BMI and HbA1c, yet the underlying numbers are −3.4 and −2.0 against trial values of −5.7 and −4.3 for BMI, and −0.57 and −0.53 against −0.4 and −1.7 for HbA1c, in a cohort about 90 percent male against 20 to 40 percent in the trials. The verdict is a label; the comparison is neither placed on a common estimand nor given a tolerance.
problems.quote: The benchmarking was approximately successful even though the population of the present study

problems.evidence: Three distinct sources of error are present at once: the scientific question about surgery, two different target trials that answer different questions about when randomization occurs, and an emulation that fails on the unrecorded date of consideration. The conclusion attributes the residual threat to that missing date, but no decomposition separates it from the protocol compromise of switching between trial 1 and trial 2 or from the estimation error visible in the −12.0 to 14.0 interval.
problems.quote: Though we avoided some of the potential biases in previous observational analyses, the validity of our effect estimates is still threatened, especially by a lack of information about the date of consideration of bariatric surgery.

papers.title: Emulating Hypothetical Target Trials of the Broad-Spectrum T2 Biologic Dupilumab.
papers.one_line: A correspondence arguing that an emulated trial comparing mepolizumab, benralizumab and dupilumab in uncontrolled asthma violated positivity by enrolling initiators across all eosinophil strata, including counts below the thresholds at which two of the three agents are approved.
papers.what_was_done: A published emulation comparing three asthma biologics is challenged on two design points. Because efficacy of all three agents rises with eosinophil count and all three are approved for the eosinophilic phenotype, a real randomized trial of the comparison would enroll only eosinophilic patients; the emulation instead included initiators at every level of eosinophilia, so some patients could not plausibly have been assigned to mepolizumab or benralizumab. Second, the exposure-defining covariate is ambiguous: eosinophilia was categorized as at least one count of 300 per microliter or above, at least one count between 150 and 300, and at least one count below 150, which leaves the assignment of a patient with counts of 30, 250 and 480 in the year before initiation undetermined. Because many of these patients had an exacerbation treated with oral corticosteroids during that year, the measured count is expected to move within the same patient across the lookback window. A sensitivity analysis restricted to baseline counts of 300 per microliter or above produced similar exacerbation rates for dupilumab and benralizumab, unlike the primary comparison. No new data are presented.

problems.evidence: The unsupported region is named concretely: patients with counts below the approval thresholds for mepolizumab and benralizumab, who could not receive two of the three compared strategies. The original analysis reported matching on baseline covariates, and the objection is that balance diagnostics do not reveal that an entire eosinophil stratum has no plausible counterfactual assignment.
problems.quote: emulation of a hypothetical target trial comparing these three biologic agents needs to ensure equipoise when comparing therapies to avoid a violation of the concept of

problems.evidence: A laboratory value with real within-patient variability is collapsed into three categories by an at-least-one-count rule, which leaves a patient with counts of 30, 250 and 480 in the preceding year unclassifiable from the published definition. The classified variable enters the analysis as a fixed stratum, and its error is neither quantified nor propagated.
problems.quote: Given this definition, it is unclear what category, as an example, a patient with three eosinophil count measures in the year before therapy with one of 30/µl, another of 250/µl, and another of 480/µl would fall.

problems.evidence: The stratifying value depends on which point in a one-year lookback window is used, and corticosteroid treatment of exacerbations during that year moves the count. Nothing outcome-blind fixes the window length or the summary rule, and the objection is that the choice determines which stratum a patient lands in.
problems.quote: it is likely that an individual’s eosinophil categories would vary during the year before biologic therapy initiation

problems.evidence: Eligibility for the two antieosinophilic strategies turns on a threshold count, but the emulation admitted initiators across all levels of eosinophilia, so patients who would have been ineligible in the target trial are indistinguishable in the data from those who met the criterion. The sensitivity analysis restricted to counts of 300 or above changed the dupilumab versus benralizumab comparison, which shows the misclassification was consequential.
problems.quote: Thus, they might have included patients with eosinophil counts below the threshold at which mepolizumab and benralizumab would be approved.

problems.evidence: The critique is aimed at a study that carried the target trial label and still failed the positivity requirement and left its exposure-defining covariate ambiguous. The label did not signal a lower assumption burden, and the correspondence has to argue the specifics because nothing in the designation did that work.
problems.quote: Although an emulation of a hypothetical target trial is important in improving the quality of observational trials, it is still fraught with limitations, like any nonexperimental study
